The vaccine arrived in January. By March, the clinic had administered ten thousand doses. Dr. Patel worked sixteen-hour days. Her staff worked longer. They set up tables in the parking lot. They vaccinated people in their cars. The line stretched around the block every morning. Some people drove two hours to get there. Others walked. An elderly man showed up at six a.m. in a wheelchair. He had been waiting eleven months. He cried when he got the shot. His nurse cried too. The logistics were brutal. The paperwork was worse. Supply chains broke down twice. Freezers failed once. But they kept going. Public health is not glamorous work. It does not make headlines until something goes wrong. Dr. Patel does not care about headlines. She cares about the next patient in line. That is enough.
